## High article potential

_The note-taker's per-doc rating; the ranked, cross-doc plan is in articles/CANDIDATES.md._

- [2026-11-09 27b-arms-kld](findings/quality/2026-11-09-1825-27b-arms-kld.md) — How a KLD quant comparison got a scorer bug fixed and what it says about quant ordering: Q6_K closest, IQ4R-L-V4 between Q6 and Q4_K_XL, MXFP4 about 7-8x further on any engine, and q8_0 KV showing no cost **Hook:** A Q8_0 re-run scored a KL floor of 0.1106 before a string-keying fix and 0.00176 after, so the bug made an identical model look about 60x noisier
- [2026-11-06 ornith-manual](findings/workers/2026-11-06-0930-ornith-manual.md) — running a free local worker day to day: the knob that does nothing (effort), a prompt that helps one profile and hurts another, and where the output must not be trusted **Hook:** Ornith's effort setting changed nothing: low, medium, high, xhigh and an invalid value all gave identical token counts at temperature zero
- [2026-11-05 ornith-use-cases](findings/workers/2026-11-05-0814-ornith-use-cases.md) — what to hand a free local model: a task whose output a script can check, versus anything needing completeness or judgement; retyping is the clearest cliff **Hook:** Ornith split a 6,000-token document with a script in 39 seconds and lost no lines, but retyping the same text took 480 seconds and two more runs were cut at 600-720 seconds
- [2026-11-04 sly-radiance-ornith-vs-haiku-high-effort](findings/workers/2026-11-04-2207-sly-radiance-ornith-vs-haiku-high-effort.md) — where a free local 35B worker can be trusted and where it cannot: counting and quoting from long documents versus judging them, measured with blind grading **Hook:** At 117k tokens across seven reports Ornith put 32 of 35 numbers on the exact cited line and invented none, but its verdicts on four deep reports scored 8 and 9 of 12 against Haiku's 12 and 11
- [2026-11-04 ornith15-radiance-vs-sly-35b-27b](findings/radiance/2026-11-04-1746-ornith15-radiance-vs-sly-35b-27b.md) — Same card, same MoE family: one vLLM backend flag moves a 35B MoE from 16.6 to 110 tok/s decode, and a native runtime reaches 220 tok/s; the article would be where the decode gap actually comes from **Hook:** Switching only the vLLM MoE backend from EMULATION to triton_unfused takes Qwen3.5-35B MXFP4 on Sly from 16.6 to 110.2 tok/s decode at 10k
- [2026-11-04 qwen35-35b-a3b-radiance-config-alternatives](research/vllm/2026-11-04-1702-qwen35-35b-a3b-radiance-config-alternatives.md) — Our own report said no 35B could reach 200 tok/s on this card, and a model our search had missed proved it wrong **Hook:** One vLLM flag took our 35B-A3B from 16.6 to 110 tok/s at 10k, and a model our search had missed then measured 219.8 tok/s on the same card
- [2026-11-04 qwen35-35b-a3b-vllm-rocm-decode-gap](research/vllm/2026-11-04-1630-qwen35-35b-a3b-vllm-rocm-decode-gap.md) — A 35B MoE ran about 5x slower than the 27B because a fallback backend dequantizes every expert on every step **Hook:** On our R9700 the 35B-A3B decodes at 14-17 tok/s against 74-94 for the 27B, because the MoE falls back to an emulation path that expands all 256 experts to bf16 on each step (root cause confirmed by a later measurement)
- [2026-10-31 redhat191-sharp-w208-blind](findings/agentic/2026-10-31-0000-redhat191-sharp-w208-blind.md) — Could feed a piece on why decode tok/s misleads for agentic workloads and how lossy speculative acceptance can lock a model into loops. **Hook:** Cactus delta 0.5 decoded 65% faster per token yet took 2.4x the wall time, generating 4.1x the tokens, 49% of them inside loops.
- [2026-10-31 reasoning-replay-sharp-template-cactus-loops](findings/agentic/2026-10-31-1745-reasoning-replay-sharp-template-cactus-loops.md) — Feeds a piece on speculative-decoding failure modes: how a lossy acceptance rule builds an absorbing repetition loop, and which fixes remove it and which only shorten it. **Hook:** On 1.8.1 any drafted token with target p >= 0.5 is accepted with certainty under Cactus delta 0.5, so a loop has no exit: 0 of 3 top loops escaped and all hit the 64k cap.
- [2026-10-31 agentic-thinking-volume-and-levers](findings/agentic/2026-10-31-1640-agentic-thinking-volume-and-levers.md) — Feeds a piece on what drives token cost in agentic coding runs on local models: trajectory length and compaction, not the sampler or the weights. **Hook:** Thinking per tool call stayed at 3.0-3.6k characters across the W2-08 arms; the step count (70 to 155) drove the total.
- [2026-10-31 kv-cache-quantization-long-context](research/models-sampling/2026-10-31-1630-kv-cache-quantization-long-context.md) — Quantized KV at long context: a kernel accumulation bug, not the 8-bit format, is the depth cliff, and that changes what a depth test must measure **Hook:** On Hopper FA3, fp8 KV needle recall at 128k fell from 91% to 13% until a two-level accumulation fix, so the 8-bit format was not the failure (CLAIMED, vLLM blog)
- [2026-10-30 vllm-redhat-sly191-d0-dflash-depth](findings/vllm/2026-10-30-2232-vllm-redhat-sly191-d0-dflash-depth.md) — lossless speculative decoding on RDNA4: why an external 7-token drafter beats the model's own MTP head at every depth but one tie, and why a relaxed-acceptance setting is a speed lever only for the drafter **Hook:** At delta 0 the model's own MTP head decodes 62.8 tok/s at 10k against 100.2 for an external DFlash2 drafter, and the lossy relaxation that should help MTP moves its acceptance by only -5 to +8 percent
- [2026-10-30 dpf-brief-fix-heretic-vs-redhat](findings/agentic/2026-10-30-1552-dpf-brief-fix-heretic-vs-redhat.md) — Could feed an article on agentic coding with local models: a lossy speculative-decode acceptance rule turned a reasoning model into a repetition loop, plus the template replay that made the same brief 8.7x slower. **Hook:** At the Sly default Cactus delta 0.5, 777 of 1,067 decode windows (72.8%) were repetition loops and 0 of 3 briefs finished in 3 h; delta 0 removed the loops on this task.
- [2026-10-30 vllm-redhat-mxfp4-depth-transposed](findings/radiance/2026-10-30-0900-vllm-redhat-mxfp4-depth-transposed.md) — Why a speculative-decoding speed-up measured at 10k depth (6.8x) shrinks to 4.6x at 100k on one R9700, and how much of that is acceptance versus step cost **Hook:** DFlash2 decodes 122.27 tok/s at 10k against 18.03 with no speculation, but at 100k the same method gives 87.36 against 18.87 (6.78x falling to 4.63x)
- [2026-10-23 vllm-gpu-fault-solved-hip-kernarg](findings/vllm/2026-10-23-0023-vllm-gpu-fault-solved-hip-kernarg.md) — a random GPU memory fault on ROCm turned out to be a corrupted kernel-argument pointer, fixed by one environment variable that moves kernel arguments to host memory **Hook:** A random HSA memory fault that hit about 12 of about 21 boots disappeared when kernel arguments were moved from device memory written over PCIe to host memory (HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0)
- [2026-10-22 vllm-sly-mxfp4-dflash](findings/vllm/2026-10-22-1406-vllm-sly-mxfp4-dflash.md) — speculative decoding on RDNA4 through vLLM: a drafter multiplies decode 4-5.6x without slowing prefill, but acceptance rather than depth sets the speed, and an image's lookup draft confounds the attribution **Hook:** A drafter lifts single-stream decode from 33.8 to 136.6 tok/s at 8k and from 17.9 to 100.5 at 136k, with prefill unchanged within 3 percent
- [2026-10-22 vllm-sly-mxfp4-depth](findings/vllm/2026-10-22-1324-vllm-sly-mxfp4-depth.md) — a 27B on RDNA4 under vLLM Sly radiance is a prefill engine with a weak decode: the prefill-decode asymmetry, prefix caching for agent loops, and the intermittent GPU memory fault to watch for **Hook:** Sly radiance 1.6.0 prefills 2,845 tok/s at 8k and still 1,500 tok/s at 136k, yet decodes only 33.8 tok/s at 8k without a drafter and 17.9 at 136k
- [2026-09-12 vllm-window-budgets-and-rocm-knobs](findings/vllm/2026-09-12-1535-vllm-window-budgets-and-rocm-knobs.md) — on a hybrid Gated-DeltaNet model, speculative decoding can cost more KV window than the attention itself, and the fp8 KV cache the list recommends changes nothing: why the window budget is set by mamba state, not attention **Hook:** At a 36,864-token window MTP-8 reserved 30 KV blocks for recurrent-state rollback against 23 for all attention, and fp8 KV changed the pool by exactly zero tokens
- [2026-09-12 vllm-radiance-r9700-evaluation](findings/radiance/2026-09-12-1055-vllm-radiance-r9700-evaluation.md) — The tuned 2x vLLM is a drafter stack rather than kernels, and the engine ranking flips by workload: radiance generates code faster, llama.cpp reviews it faster, and the depth story was a fixture artifact **Hook:** At the same ~8k depth radiance decodes generated code 26 % faster than llama.cpp+MTP, and review prose 49 % slower
- [2026-09-11 vllm-qwen38-27b-int4](findings/vllm/2026-09-11-2047-vllm-qwen38-27b-int4.md) — why vLLM's default attention backend collapses decode on a head_dim-256 hybrid model on RDNA4: a 4-workgroup decode grid and a per-kernel dispatch floor **Hook:** The default ROCm attention backend launches its decode kernel with a grid of (1, 4), 4 workgroups on a 64-CU card, and decode falls to 2.8 tok/s at 32k
- [driver-upgrade-runbook](guides/driver-upgrade-runbook.md) — a driver upgrade that changed nothing it touched on paper still reversed a tuning result: two GPU stacks over one kernel driver, with the shell and pipeline traps met on the way **Hook:** A ROCm upgrade installed 52 packages and removed none, yet a prefill tuning went from a 1.57x win to a 47% loss, and the install script went silent because head closed a pipe
- [2026-09-10 hipfire-bench-rocm713-final](findings/hipfire/2026-09-10-0100-hipfire-bench-rocm713-final.md) — A split verdict on a fast new engine: it decodes faster at short context but prefills slower, and the prefill loss is a host-CPU bottleneck that configuration only partly fixes. **Hook:** hipfire decodes a coding turn at 150 tok/s against llama.cpp's 64, yet its 70k prefill runs at 293 tok/s against 595, and the profile puts the bottleneck on one host CPU thread at 89% busy while the GPU sits about half idle.
- [2026-09-10 hipfire-final-analysis](findings/hipfire/2026-09-10-0100-hipfire-final-analysis.md) — Feeds a piece on engine-evaluation traps: a dispatcher threshold, a daemon that wedges while reporting healthy, and a prefix cache that is effectively zero under multi-agent use. **Hook:** After the fixes, 7 of 19 draft-free hipfire boots (37%) faulted on a GPU memory fault, and /health kept answering ok on the wedged daemon.
- [2026-09-02 mrcr-v2-qwen38-27b-q6k](findings/quality/2026-09-02-1437-mrcr-v2-qwen38-27b-q6k.md) — Local 27B long-context retrieval at 131K on one 32 GB card: 0.850 with failures that are counting errors rather than context loss, plus the pitfalls (silent context shift, bench-figure underprediction) that a planner must avoid **Hook:** 86% of the 35 samples scored at least 0.90 and none fell between 0.10 and 0.90: when the model fails at 131K it reproduces a wrong instance flawlessly
- [2026-07-27 runner-benchmark-unified](findings/quality/2026-07-27-0000-runner-benchmark-unified.md) — Gate-green is not a quality proxy: the local model with the most favourable operational numbers silently overwrote working translations, and run-to-run variance is larger than any model or harness difference **Hook:** ThinkingCap-27B-Q6_K_L passed the runner gates on every sample and still overwrote four working Hungarian translations with English in 4 of 5 samples; the judge placed it in the bottom tier
- [2026-07-19 ornith-35b-gemma-4-31b-configs](research/models-sampling/2026-07-19-1821-ornith-35b-gemma-4-31b-configs.md) — The same dense 31B model device-losts RADV on Vulkan at depth and completes on ROCm, so a driver bug picks the backend **Hook:** Gemma-4-31B device-lost the Vulkan driver at about 65k tokens of prefill and took the desktop down; the ROCm build ran a 140k prefill clean but decoded about 6x slower
- [2026-07-16 spec-draft-p-min-mtp](research/llamacpp/2026-07-16-1016-spec-draft-p-min-mtp.md) — A source-reading conclusion refuted by measurement on the real build: a how-we-verify-spec-decode-knobs piece **Hook:** Raising --spec-draft-p-min to 0.99 on MTP lifts acceptance from 69% to 100% yet drops decode from 159.9 to 106.5 t/s (MEASURED, 35B-A3B, b9950)
- [2026-07-16 mtp-sampler-tax](findings/llamacpp/2026-07-16-0927-mtp-sampler-tax.md) — Why a sampler setting that changes no tokens still costs 29% decode: a fixed ~2 ms host tax per token, which bites hardest on the fastest speculative step (Amdahl), not draft rejection **Hook:** presence_penalty 0.01, too small to change any token, still cut decode from 161.1 to 115.1 tok/s (−28.6%) with a byte-identical reply and identical draft acceptance (69.06%)
- [2026-07-16 27b-coding-model-on-one-amd-card](articles/2026-07-16-27b-coding-model-on-one-amd-card.md) — Already the published 27B write-up; can feed a planned piece on free speedups for local coding models on AMD (MTP build choice plus a thinking cap). **Hook:** The MTP build decodes at 70.3 tok/s against 31.1 tok/s for the non-MTP build (2.25x), with the same 100% deterministic accuracy.
- [2026-07-16 assumptions-vs-reality](articles/2026-07-16-assumptions-vs-reality.md) — Feeds a piece on catching your own wrong causal story in local-LLM benchmarking, with the four assumptions as structure. **Hook:** --reasoning-budget 0 is uncapped on this build: 1,736 thinking tokens, more than the 1,262 of its own 2048 cap.
- [2026-07-16 reasoning-budget-free-lunch](articles/2026-07-16-reasoning-budget-free-lunch.md) — Feeds a general piece on reasoning-model serving defaults: capping thinking as the cheapest lever, with the untested depth caveat. **Hook:** Capping thinking at 1024 tokens cut tokens and latency 40-55% with 100% deterministic accuracy, and runaways fell from 7.1% to 0%.
- [2026-07-14 hardest-tasks-27b-vs-35b](findings/quality/2026-07-14-0000-hardest-tasks-27b-vs-35b.md) — Sampling hygiene and reasoning budget beat quant shopping on hard coding tasks: the vendor coding recipe wins, a 4x thinking budget buys nothing on the 27B, and presence_penalty costs decode via a fixed host tax **Hook:** Quadrupling the 27B thinking budget from 4096 to 16384 moved TS quality by +0.3 pts (t=0.37) for +60 s per reply, refuting the truncated-thinking hypothesis this repo's own research had argued
- [2026-07-15 qwen36-sampling-thinking-budget-variance](research/models-sampling/2026-07-15-1000-qwen36-sampling-thinking-budget-variance.md) — Thinking budget versus sampling: why a hard-coding eval kept hitting its reasoning cap while the sampling was already vendor-correct **Hook:** Our thinking budget of 4096 was saturated in every cell (3629-4095 tokens), about 8x below Qwen's 32,768 recommendation, while the sampling already matched the vendor's coding recipe
- [2026-07-13 27b-quality-at-depth-detailed](findings/quality/2026-07-13-1657-27b-quality-at-depth-detailed.md) — The same 120 frozen answers scored 24-33% on a broken grader and 67-79% after a CPU-only re-grade, so the failure was the ruler, not the model **Hook:** A 27B model was graded below Haiku because vitest never ran; re-grading the same saved answers on CPU put it in the Haiku-to-Sonnet band
- [2026-07-14 hardest-tasks-27b-vs-35b-pre-summary](findings/quality/2026-07-14-0000-hardest-tasks-27b-vs-35b-pre-summary.md) — The model vendor's own thinking-mode preset is the worst of the settings we tested, costing about 16 points on hard TypeScript; the folklore temp 0.3 is also significantly worse **Hook:** Qwen's documented thinking-mode preset cost about 16 points on hard coding work, and the folklore temperature 0.3 was significantly worse than 0.6
- [2026-07-13 27b-quality-tuning](findings/quality/2026-07-13-1138-27b-quality-tuning.md) — A thinking-budget cap is the master knob: capping reasoning at about 1024 tokens cuts tokens roughly in half with no verified accuracy loss and removes runaways, and the earlier MTP-runaway story was the uncapped budget **Hook:** Capping thinking at 1024 tokens kept 100% deterministic accuracy and removed all runaways (7.1% uncapped), while --reasoning-budget 0 turned out to mean uncapped, not no-think
- [2026-07-13 27b-serving-substrate](findings/llamacpp/2026-07-13-0733-27b-serving-substrate.md) — Prefix reuse, not raw prefill speed, makes agentic coding turns viable on one 32 GB card; the 'slow prefill' was a small-prompt artifact **Hook:** A warm 32K prefix drops time-to-first-token from 42.66 s to 3.12 s (13.7x), while the earlier ~200 tok/s prefill was an artifact of 51-99-token prompts
- [2026-07-12 27b-finetune-quality](findings/quality/2026-07-12-1736-27b-finetune-quality.md) — Same architecture, four fine-tunes: the thinking spread is 7.6x and the built-in truncation flag misses the runaways, so quality and cost differ by training data alone **Hook:** On one identical hybrid architecture, headline-task thinking ranges from 607 to 4612 tokens across fine-tunes, and the built-in truncation flag reported False for all three runaways
- [2026-07-11 deep-context-35b](findings/llamacpp/2026-07-11-2200-deep-context-35b.md) — When speculative decoding hurts: on one 32 GB card, deep-context requests with short answers lose wall time even as decode speeds up by a third **Hook:** MTP lifts 200K decode from 61.0 to 82.4 tok/s (+35.1%), yet the 200K request takes 16.7 s longer (158.1 to 174.8 s wall) because prefill dominates
- [2026-07-11 campaign-combo35b](findings/llamacpp/2026-07-11-1844-campaign-combo35b.md) — MTP is a single-user win and a parallel-agent loss on the same card, so the right serving config depends on how many agents share the GPU. **Hook:** On a 35B MoE, MTP adds 33% to single-stream decode and takes 8% off each stream at four concurrent agents.
- [2026-07-10 rdna4-r9700-tuning-optimum](findings/llamacpp/2026-07-10-1810-rdna4-r9700-tuning-optimum.md) — The RDNA4 tuning map: Vulkan is the backend, MTP is the biggest decode lever, the -ub and -b optimum is model-specific, and vLLM and transformers are not usable on this card at this build. **Hook:** On the R9700 the same 27B model decodes 2.3x faster with MTP on Vulkan (73.5 vs 31.7 tok/s), while vLLM cannot load it at all.
- [2026-07-10 rdna4-llamacpp-ollama-backend-tuning](research/llamacpp/2026-07-10-0000-rdna4-llamacpp-ollama-backend-tuning.md) — Batch-size folklore and build regressions on RDNA4: how a single commit or a misread ub knob can make a card look half as fast, supporting a tuning article **Hook:** Our own sweep: 35B prefill rises from 529 tok/s at ub32 to 1489 at ub512, against the ub 32/64 folklore; a single llama.cpp commit (issue #12764) also halved gfx1201 prefill (~2147 to ~1260 tok/s)
- [historical](guides/vllm/historical.md) — a version-scoped workaround that became a generic rule: how one environment variable ended a memory fault on RDNA4, and why the repo had to demote it to history **Hook:** One environment variable, HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0, ended a GPU memory fault that hit about 12 of 21 boots, and the repo had carried it as a rule for every ROCm engine
- [known-issues](guides/vllm/known-issues.md) — A vLLM image's silent defaults on RDNA4 (a slow MoE backend and a lossy acceptance transform) surfaced only by measuring failures, feeding a how-things-break piece on local inference **Hook:** The default MoE backend EMULATION decodes at 16.6 tok/s at 10k, while the triton_unfused override reaches 110.2 tok/s (MEASURED, DFlash K=7, sly 1.9.1)
